strong_dependence_arm.purpose: Test the upper bound under dependence far above the corpus level (corpus lag-1 max 0.0256).
strong_dependence_arm.generator: block-constant Dirichlet emission, concentration 0.01 (10x more concentrated than the 0.1 used elsewhere)
strong_dependence_arm.measured_induced_lag1: 0.95-0.999 depending on block size (far above the 0.05 threshold)
strong_dependence_arm.prediction_in_advance: coverage falls below 1.0 for at least the largest B at the smallest n; radius too small by ~sqrt(B) once within-block dependence is real

outcome.coverage: 1.000 in all 32 cells, i.e. the pre-registered decline did NOT appear
outcome.MECHANISM__why_that_is_not_a_pass: The bound is tv_hat + radius. Under this dependence the ESTIMATE itself inflates: at n=2791, true TV 0.10, the median tv_hat rises 0.121 (iid) -> 0.482 (B=64) -> 1.000 (B=1024). An upper bound that is already 5-10x the truth cannot fail to cover, so coverage 1.0 here is UNINFORMATIVE rather than reassuring.
outcome.direct_measurement: median eps_hi vs true TV, n=2791 / n=100000, iid vs B in {64,1024,10000}: see strong_dependence_arm.mechanism_table

strong_dependence_arm.honest_conclusion: The bound does not become INVALID under strong dependence; it becomes UNINFORMATIVE. Coverage 1.0 is achieved by the estimate inflating, not by the radius tracking the true sampling variability. This is consistent with the paper's own C2 result that the certificate dies as resolution grows, and it must NOT be presented as "the bound is robust under dependence".
strong_dependence_arm.note: SUPERSEDED as a separate experiment: independently measured, the ORIGINAL dependent arm (conc=0.1) already exercises indicator lag-1 of 0.47/0.82/0.9997/0.9999 at B=2/8/2000/10000 versus an i.i.d. baseline of 0.031. This arm therefore repeats an experiment already run. Its value is limited to the direct estimate-inflation measurement (tv_hat 0.121->0.482->1.000 against true TV 0.10).

runner.modification: 4 path constants only (PROJECT_ROOT, two H5 candidates, sys.path src); verified by line-by-line diff

caveat__what_this_does_not_show: The radius 0.5*sqrt(m/n)+0.5*sqrt(2 ln(2/alpha)/n) is a pure function of n: identical between the i.i.d. and dependent arms at every n, and invariant to block size B. At n=2791 it is 0.0816, i.e. 1.63x the true TV of 0.05, so coverage 1.000 there is trivially guaranteed and carries no information. Only the large-n cells (n=100000, radius 0.0136 < true 0.05) are informative. Any citation of this calibration must report the true-TV-to-radius ratio per cell.
